title: Design a cost-optimized architecture
objective: Compare costs and constraints based on usage volume, access frequency, availability requirements, and operational burden.

sections.title: Relating Costs to Usage Patterns
paragraphs: Cost optimization is not about choosing the least expensive service. Decision-makers distinguish between continuous usage, variable workloads, predictable usage periods, and stoppable processing, then compare options that meet performance and availability requirements.

sections.title: Choose a storage destination based on access frequency and retention period
paragraphs: In S3, you can choose a storage class based on the requirements for frequently read data, infrequent access, or archiving. Lifecycle configurations can transition data to another class or expire it, but you should also evaluate retrieval time and minimum storage duration.

sections.title: Reassessing Design Changes Based on Quality and Cost
paragraphs: When changing the design of a reservation service, compare not only the monthly cost but also the RTO, RPO, latency, operational effort, and data-retention obligations in the same table. Well-Architected provides a framework for examining the advantages and disadvantages of design decisions.

checkpoints.prompt: A data platform specialist stores audit files in Amazon S3 that must be retained for 7 years by law. They are rarely accessed under normal circumstances, but once an audit begins, each individual file must be retrieved within 1 minute. What is the appropriate approach when reviewing storage costs?

choices.text: Consider infrequent-access classes that allow immediate retrieval, and compare retrieval without restoration, minimum storage duration, and retrieval charges against the retention requirements.
choices.explanation: This lets you compare storage and retrieval costs for candidates that satisfy both the low access frequency and short retrieval-time requirements.

choices.text: Choose the archive with the lowest storage cost and send a restoration request on the day of the audit.
choices.explanation: Choosing based only on storage cost may fail to meet the requirement to retrieve files within 1 minute.

choices.text: Continue encrypting the data at rest, then delete older files before the retention deadline to reduce costs.
choices.explanation: Encryption does not justify shortening the retention period. This would violate the retention obligation.

checkpoints.prompt: An overnight image-regeneration batch can record its progress and resume from another instance. The processing must finish by 6:00 a.m., but it is acceptable for some runs to be interrupted as long as they can resume by the deadline. Which option is appropriate for reducing costs?

choices.text: Process all work on a single Spot Instance without measuring the time required to resume after an interruption.
choices.explanation: Even for interruptible work, you need a way to resume that can meet the deadline, as well as an estimate of the time required.

choices.text: Reserve enough On-Demand capacity for peak demand throughout the day and night, keeping it running even when it is not executing work.
choices.explanation: This is operationally simple, but you incur costs for capacity used only at night. It does not take advantage of the fact that the work can be interrupted.

choices.text: Consider Spot for interruptible work and measure the time required to resume. Also plan for On-Demand capacity if the deadline approaches.
choices.explanation: This reduces costs by taking advantage of the work’s interruptibility while providing an alternative to ensure that the processing deadline is met.

checkpoints.prompt: There is a proposal to switch the reservation service’s DB to a smaller instance to reduce monthly costs. There is a contract requiring the p95 latency for confirming reservations to remain at or below 400 milliseconds, and traffic at the end of the month is normally twice the usual volume. Which conditions should be verified in the design review?

choices.text: Verify that average CPU utilization is low during weekday daytime hours and that the monthly cost will be lower than it is now.
choices.explanation: Average utilization and cost alone do not show whether the response-time requirement can be met during the month-end peak.

choices.text: Under a month-end-equivalent load, verify response time, error rate, available DB capacity, and recovery procedures, then compare the proposal with the current design, including any additional costs.
choices.explanation: This allows you to determine, based on the requirements, whether the less expensive configuration meets the necessary quality standards and whether it can be rolled back if it fails.

choices.text: Verify only that the number of DB instances and the storage capacity are the same.
choices.explanation: Even with the same number of instances and storage capacity, available CPU, memory, and input/output headroom may differ, affecting response time.
